name: Vibe-Trading

hlido_opinion.headline: An open-source finance research agent that turns natural-language market questions into runnable, inspectable backtests — and, unusually for this category, draws an explicit line at live trading instead of blurring it.
hlido_opinion.body: Vibe-Trading is a research harness, not a trading bot, and the surface is disciplined about saying so. The pitch is concrete: a prompt becomes a route through data sources, strategies, backtests and a report, and the example shown is a real command (vibe-trading run -p "Backtest BTC-USDT 20/50 MA for 2024") returning a run card with a return and a max drawdown rather than a screenshot of a dashboard. The four-step research loop — route, ground, test, deliver — is stated with what each step does, and the stated output of every run is a card with exports, tool traces and caveats, which is the right artifact for research you may have to defend later. Breadth is substantial on paper: eleven backtest engines across A-shares, global, Indian, Korean and Vietnamese equities, crypto, futures, forex, cross-market composites and options; preset swarm teams (investment committee, quant desk, risk review, macro); persistent memory, session search, editable skills and context compression; and a shadow-account feature that parses broker journals to extract implicit rules and run counterfactuals. Install is a published PyPI package. The strongest single thing on the page is the BOUNDARY section: it states that the product is for research, simulation and backtesting, that any live trading is opt-in and read-only by default, that it runs only through a broker you authorise yourself, within limits you set, and that you can halt it instantly. In a category where the incentive runs hard the other way, that is a deliberate restraint and it should count. The caution is that everything above is read off a marketing page. The 36.7k star count is displayed by the vendor and was not independently verified here; no backtest was reproduced; and the gap between eleven engines advertised and eleven engines that work well is exactly the gap a public-surface review cannot close. Backtest tooling also carries an inherent hazard this page does not address: nothing on the captured surface discusses look-ahead bias, survivorship bias or overfitting, which are the failure modes that make a good-looking backtest worthless.

tier_rationale: STEADY (76) because the product is open source with a published install path, an unusually specific and inspectable research loop, broad declared market coverage, and an explicit, well-drafted boundary around live trading that most of this category avoids. It is held out of VITAL because none of the engines or figures were verified here, the star count is vendor-displayed, and the surface says nothing about the statistical hazards (look-ahead, survivorship, overfitting) that decide whether a backtest means anything.
what_it_does_well: States an explicit boundary — research and simulation by default, live trading opt-in and read-only through a broker you authorise, haltable instantly — in a category that usually blurs exactly this line
Every run is designed to leave an inspectable trail: run cards, exports, tool traces and caveats rather than a bare number
Concrete, reproducible-looking examples (a real CLI invocation returning a return and a max drawdown) instead of dashboard screenshots
Broad declared coverage: eleven backtest engines across A-shares, global, Indian, Korean and Vietnamese equities, crypto, futures, forex, composites and options
Open source with a published PyPI install (pip install vibe-trading-ai) and visible documentation, tutorials and an alpha library
The shadow-account feature — parsing broker journals to surface implicit rules and run counterfactuals — is a genuinely original idea in this space
what_it_fails_at: No independent verification of the 36.7k star figure, which is rendered by the vendor's own page
Nothing on the captured surface addresses look-ahead bias, survivorship bias or overfitting — the hazards that determine whether any backtest is meaningful
Eleven engines is a breadth claim with no evidence of depth or accuracy in any one of them
No pricing, support or maintenance commitment is stated, as is common but still material for open source used on money decisions
No backtest was reproduced in this review; every performance figure shown is illustrative vendor copy
best_for: Quantitative researchers who want a natural-language front end to backtesting while keeping the trail inspectable
Analysts covering Asian equity markets, where the declared A-share, Indian, Korean and Vietnamese coverage is unusual
Anyone who wants research tooling that is explicit about not executing trades for them
Python-comfortable users willing to validate the engines themselves before trusting a result
not_recommended_for: Anyone looking for a trading bot — the product deliberately is not one, and says so
Users who would act on a backtest without independently checking for look-ahead or survivorship bias
Institutions needing vendor support, SLAs or audited methodology
Non-technical users: the whole interface is a CLI and a Python package
red_flags: A backtesting product whose public surface never mentions look-ahead bias, survivorship bias or overfitting — the three ways a backtest lies
Headline traction (36.7k stars) is displayed by the vendor on its own page and was not independently confirmed in this review

compared_to.verdict_diff: CrewAI is a general multi-agent framework you would build a finance workflow on top of; Vibe-Trading ships the finance workflow — data routing, eleven backtest engines, preset research teams — already assembled. Choose CrewAI to build your own, Vibe-Trading to start from a domain-shaped harness.

OpenHands is an open agent harness for software tasks with a broad community; Vibe-Trading applies the same harness idea to market research with domain tooling and an explicit trading boundary. Different domains, comparable openness.

Langroid is a general-purpose multi-agent programming framework; Vibe-Trading is an end-user research product with finance engines built in. Pick Langroid to construct agents, Vibe-Trading to run market research today.

evidence_urls.claim: Open-source finance research agent installed via pip install vibe-trading-ai
Four-stage inspectable loop: route, ground, test, deliver, returning run cards with tool traces and caveats
Eleven backtest engines across A-shares, global, Indian, Korean and Vietnamese equities, crypto, futures, forex, composites and options
Live trading is opt-in and read-only by default, runs only through a broker you authorise, within your limits, haltable instantly
Shadow Account parses broker journals to extract implicit rules and run counterfactual backtests

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Vibe-Trading is driven by a CLI (vibe-trading run -p "...", vibe-trading --swarm-run ...) and distributed as a Python package, so another agent can invoke it as a subprocess and parse the run card it emits. Editable skills and session search are advertised. No API or MCP endpoint appears on the captured surface.
